paper_verdict.estimator_family: dynamic panel fixed effects (two-way FE with lagged dependent variable, country-clustered SE; not GMM)
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Exposure DIGI_std is a PCA composite standardized to mean 0/SD 1 and the outcome LAP_level is in thousands of PPP$ per worker (level), so units differ from growth or log specifications. Only 17 Asia-Pacific economies. The DIGI_std coefficient in model 5 is conditional on the DIGI x GREEN interaction in the same model (marginal effect of DIGI at GREEN=0). Authors state DIGI and GREEN are treated as exogenous and results are conditional associations; Nickell bias acknowledged and not corrected.

estimates.note: Table 4 col (5) LAP. Note states robust SE clustered by country in parentheses, so SE type is right. Observations 198, Countries 17. Text: beta = 0.985, p = 0.090. Coefficient is conditional on the interaction term being in the model.

Table 4 col (5) LAP, 1.685 *** with SE 0.633, N=198, 17 countries. This is the interaction coefficient, not the marginal effect of digital technology alone; consider excluding or treating separately from main-effect estimates.

paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Coefficients are System GMM (xtbond2) levels of ICT indicators on real GDP growth rate (TX_PIB) in percent. Estimates are measured in raw units of heterogeneous ICT indicators (internet use, mobile and fixed subscriptions, ICT goods import share). Small samples (OECD 147-156 obs, MENA 73 obs; 18 OECD and 14 MENA countries listed in footnotes, but the number of countries actually used is not reported). Several MENA specifications show AR2 p < 0.10 and Sargan p near 0.05-0.07, and a MENA L.log_PIB of 1.64 in Table 8 spec 2 suggests instability. Text defines the lagged dependent as TX_PIB(t-1) while tables label it L.log_PIB; unit ambiguity. MENA is a mixed-income group (Gulf high-income plus middle/low income), so income group is not homogeneous. Interaction rows are product-term coefficients whose own main effects are in the same column.
